title: Sightseeing holidays
subtitle: go sightseeing, packed with tourists, worth visiting
summary: Talk about the places tourists visit, what you do on a sightseeing holiday, and how to describe a place.

lesson.heading: Things to see
rows: a castle
a large strong building built long ago to protect people
a palace
the large home of a king or queen
a cathedral
a very large church
a mosque
a building where Muslims go to pray
a temple
a religious building in some religions
a statue
a figure of a person or animal made of stone or metal
a fountain
water that goes up into the air, often in a square
a market
a place, often outside, where people sell things
lesson.note: The religious places here are the cathedral, the mosque and the temple.

lesson.heading: Tourist activities
rows: go sightseeing / see the sights
We went **sightseeing** almost every day.
do a bit of / a lot of sightseeing
I didn't do a lot of **sightseeing** in Warsaw.
have a look round (visit casually, on foot)
I want to **have a look round** the museum.
explore (go round a new place to see what is there)
We **explored** the flower market.
go out (leave your hotel for a restaurant, theatre, etc.)
On holiday we **went out** every night.
get lost (lose your way)
I **got lost** three times in London.
have a great / nice / terrible time
They **had a lovely time** in Venice.
buy souvenirs
We bought some dolls as **souvenirs**.
lesson.note: A souvenir is something you buy or keep to remember a place or holiday.

lesson.heading: The word place
lesson.text: **Place** can describe a building, an area, a town or a country. **Guidebooks** are books with information about places.

examples.text: We found a really nice **place** to stay.
The **guidebooks** say the Alhambra is magnificent.

lesson.heading: Describing places
lesson.text: A **magnificent** building is very good or very beautiful. A **packed** place is very crowded. A **lively** place is full of life and activity, and if there is **plenty** to do, there is a lot to do.

examples.text: The Alhambra is always **packed** with tourists in the summer.
Sao Paulo is a **lively place**, and there's **plenty** to do in the evening.
St Petersburg has lots of historic **monuments**.
examples.note: = important places built a long time ago

examples.text: The Hermitage Museum was the main **attraction** for me.
examples.note: an attraction = something that makes people want to come

lesson.heading: worth
lesson.text: We use **worth** + noun or **worth** + *-ing* to say that it is a good idea to do something or go somewhere.

examples.text: If you go to Poland, it's definitely **worth visiting** Krakow.
It's **worth hiring** a car if you go to Scotland.
Glasgow is **worth a visit** as well.

lesson.text: After *worth* use the *-ing* form: it's worth seeing, not ~~it's worth to see~~.

exercises.prompt: Which of these places are religious places?
Match each holiday activity with its meaning.

pairs.right: visit the famous places of a city
go round a new place to see what is there
visit a place casually, often on foot
buy something to remember a place

exercises.prompt: I've been in Paris for over a week now and I'm having a great ___.
exercises.explanation: We say have a great / nice / terrible time.

exercises.prompt: I did quite a lot of ___ in the first few days - the Eiffel Tower and Notre-Dame.
exercises.explanation: do a lot of sightseeing = visit a lot of famous places.

exercises.prompt: I saw the Eiffel Tower, Notre-Dame and all the usual tourist ___.
exercises.explanation: An attraction is something that makes people come to a place.

exercises.prompt: Most places are absolutely ___ with tourists at the moment.
Yesterday I decided to ___ one or two shopping areas.
exercises.hint: (go round a new place to see what is there)
exercises.explanation: explore = go round a new place to see what is there.

exercises.prompt: I got ___ on my way back to the hotel, but it didn't matter.
I ate in the hotel the first night, but now I usually ___ for dinner - the restaurants are great.
exercises.hint: (two words - leave the hotel for the evening)
exercises.explanation: go out = leave home or your hotel for a social event.

exercises.prompt: *A:* It's lively in the evening, isn't it? *B:* Yes, there's ___.
exercises.explanation: A lively place is full of life, so there is plenty (a lot) to do.

exercises.prompt: *A:* The Taj Mahal was impressive and so beautiful. *B:* Yes, it was ___.
exercises.explanation: magnificent = very good or very beautiful.

exercises.prompt: *A:* St Petersburg has many famous old places to see, hasn't it? *B:* Yes, lots of historic ___.
exercises.hint: (important places built a long time ago)
exercises.explanation: Historic monuments are important places built a long time ago.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Krakow is a good place to go to, isn't it? Put B's answer in the right order.
exercises.explanation: worth + -ing says that it is a good idea to do something.
